regime.label: The capex tax — rising real yields meet an AI-spending de-rating
regime.note: The market has flipped from rewarding AI capex to punishing it, and the pattern is now five-for-five on our own bars. Alphabet beat on revenue ($119.8B, +24% y/y) and Cloud (+82% y/y) and still fell 7.13% on 7/23 after guiding FY26 capex to $195-205B from $180-190B. Intel beat on revenue ($16.1B) and EPS ($0.42) and still fell 7.90% on 7/24 after lifting capex from $18B to 'over $20 billion' with 2027 'significantly higher'. Tesla fell 14.52% on 7/23 posting its first negative free cash flow in two years (-$1.09B) on AI/robotics spend. Oracle fell 4.19% on 7/24 to a fresh 52-week low on OpenAI concentration risk after S&P cut it to BBB-. Meta already lost ~10% on its own capex raise earlier this cycle. At the same time the 10-year Treasury yield reached 4.71%, its highest since January 2025, rising a fourth straight session on surging oil and Middle East escalation — so long-duration tech is being de-rated by the discount rate and the spending line simultaneously. June CPI was genuinely soft (headline -0.4% m/m, 3.5% y/y; core 2.6% y/y) but the FOMC is on hold at 3.50-3.75% with the next decision 7/29. Positioning implication: own dated non-AI-capex catalysts, refuse to chase what has already repriced, and hold real cash.

thesis: What changed since last tick is that the vague 'beat-and-selloff' pattern this book has been trading around resolved into something specific and tradeable: it is not that beats are being sold, it is that capex raises are being sold. Alphabet, Intel, Tesla and Oracle all confirmed it inside 48 hours and the book owned none of the three worst. That sharpens the forward call rather than just describing the past. META reports 7/29 and is the most capex-exposed name in the book, having already guided FY26 capex to $125-145B and fallen ~10% on that guidance once; holding 7.4% into that print is a coin-flip with the tape's thumb on the down side, and a coin-flip is not an edge — so META goes to zero BEFORE the event, which is precisely the action the last two reflections identified and failed to take. REGN goes to zero into its 7/30 print on genuine deterioration that got worse since last tick: US Eylea fell to $941M, -10% y/y, its first sub-$1B quarter since 2018, and Citi has now downgraded it to Neutral with a $700 target from $900 — a full downgrade, not just the target trims logged last tick. GOOGL's event has fired and it is already being sold. The anchor becomes PYPL at 14%, the cleanest anticipation setup available anywhere in the universe: the stock closed at $56.15, which is 7.2% BELOW a $60.50 all-cash bid from Stripe/Advent that PayPal's board has already rejected as too low while signalling it wants nearer $70. A stock trading below a live, already-rejected cash offer means the market is pricing real odds the deal dies — that is an unresolved spread, categorically different from a stock that has simply run. A Q2 print lands 7/28, two tick-days out, that can force either leg. PayPal has no AI-capex line to be punished for and carries the cheapest multiple in the book at 10.6x. The honest correction this tick is energy. The book framed XOM/CVX as a bet on dated 7/31 earnings, but the real driver was a geopolitical oil spike — Brent ran from ~$76.80 on 7/10 to above $100 intraday on 7/24 on a Houthi naval blockade of Saudi Arabia and tanker attacks — and the 7/31 reports cover April-June, BEFORE that spike. XOM is +14.8% since 6/30 at RSI 84; CVX sits at RSI 92, the most overbought reading in the entire 100-name universe. The move has happened, the stated catalyst cannot validate it, and Brent already fell 3.9% on Friday to settle $96.78 on US-Iran peace-talk headlines. So energy is cut to an 8% pair held explicitly as an escalation hedge, not an earnings trade. BAC is trimmed to 5% on the same discipline that retired GOOGL — its catalyst fired today, a 14% dividend raise to $0.32 that carried it to a 52-week high, with nothing scheduled until 10/14. The residual 63% cash is a regime call, not indecision: this book's measurable edge over the last two sessions came almost entirely from what it did not own.

rationale.PYPL: The anchor, raised from ~6% to 14%. [DATA] PayPal closed at $56.15 on 2026-07-24, which is 7.2% BELOW the $60.50/share all-cash bid Stripe and Advent tabled in a ~$53B proposal reported 2026-07-15 — a bid PayPal's board rejected as inadequate while signalling it wants closer to $70/share, retaining Goldman Sachs and Evercore. That gap is the entire trade. A stock trading meaningfully below a live, already-rejected cash offer means the market is pricing real odds the deal simply dies; that is an unresolved spread, which is categorically different from a stock that has merely run. [DATA] The Q2 print lands 2026-07-28 at 8:00 AM ET per the company's own IR page — two tick-days out — with Zacks consensus at ~$8.51B revenue and ~$1.28 EPS (-8.57% y/y). [ASSUMED] That print is the natural forcing event for either leg: a solid quarter strengthens the board's hand in holding out for more, a weak one hands the consortium leverage to come back. Either way the binary resolves closer, and I want the position on before it rather than after. [DATA] Critically for this regime, PayPal has no AI-capex line to be punished for and trades at a 10.64 trailing P/E, the cheapest multiple in the book. [ASSUMED] Risk acknowledged honestly: RSI(14) is 82.9 and the stock is +32.5% over 20 sessions, so the M&A leg has already partly repriced and this is not a clean untouched setup. It is sized at 14% rather than larger because a confirmed walk-away plausibly returns the stock toward the $47.37 it closed at on 2026-07-14, before the bid leaked — roughly 16% downside. [ASSUMED] Execution note: this order is deliberately left market-on-open rather than given the usual ~1% buy limit. With an unresolved bid, a weekend gap-up IS the thesis paying off rather than momentum to be chased, and a limit would leave the book sitting out the exact outcome it is positioning for. Even at $62 the spread to the board's own ~$70 framing remains intact.
rationale.LLY: Raised from ~8% to 10% — the least-extended name in the book with a genuine dated catalyst. [DATA] Q2 earnings are confirmed for 2026-08-05 with a 10:00 AM ET call, roughly 8 tick-days out, which deliberately sequences AFTER the 7/28-7/31 cluster so the book is not staking everything on the same three days. [DATA] RSI(14) is 49.3 and LLY is +6.1% over 20 sessions — it has not run, which is the entire point in a tape where XOM and CVX sit at 84 and 92. [DATA] The product cycle is live: orforglipron was approved 2026-04-01 as Foundayo, the only GLP-1 pill for weight loss without food, water or time-of-day restrictions, with Medicare Part D access at $50/month starting 2026-07-01. [DATA] Novo Nordisk sued Lilly on 2026-07-21 over allegedly misleading Zepbound/Mounjaro advertising, and Lilly said on 7/22 it stands behind its ads. [ASSUMED] I read that suit as noise rather than thesis-breaking: it attacks advertising claims, not the drugs' approvals or economics, and litigation of this type rarely resolves inside a quarter. [ASSUMED] The structural case is that a pharma franchise launching an oral GLP-1 is uncorrelated to both the AI-capex de-rating and the oil premium — the two forces driving everything else on the board right now — which is exactly the diversification this book needs. [DATA] Capped at 10% because the 42.09 trailing P/E leaves no cushion for a guidance stumble.
rationale.BAC: Trimmed hard, 10% to 5%, on precisely the discipline that retired GOOGL: the catalyst fired. [DATA] Bank of America declared a quarterly dividend of $0.32/share on 2026-07-24, up $0.04, a 14% increase payable 2026-09-25 — confirmed in the company release and the SEC 8-K, not a secondary report. [DATA] The stock closed +1.25% at 62.05 and Robinhood's 52-week-high field reads 62.275 dated 2026-07-24, meaning the high was set in this very session. [DATA] The underlying quarter was genuinely strong — net income $9.1B (+27% y/y), EPS $1.21 vs $1.12 consensus, revenue $31.6B (+15% y/y), NII ~$16B (+9% y/y) — and BAC passed the Fed's 2026 stress test released 2026-06-24. [DATA] But the next scheduled catalyst is Q3 earnings on 2026-10-14, roughly 55 tick-days away. [ASSUMED] A position with an excellent story, a same-session 52-week-high price and no forward event for two months is a momentum holding, not an anticipation holding, and this book's stated edge is the latter — the same reasoning that cut GOOGL after its print, applied consistently rather than only when the news is bad. [ASSUMED] Keeping 5% rather than zero because rising yields are a real tailwind to net interest income and this is the book's only financial.
rationale.XOM: Cut from ~6.4% to 4% and explicitly re-labelled: this is a geopolitical hedge, not an earnings trade. [DATA] The correction that matters this tick — XOM closed 156.93, up 14.8% from its 136.72 close on 2026-06-30, meaning the entire move happened in July. The 2026-07-31 earnings report covers April-June, BEFORE the spike, so the catalyst this book was nominally holding for structurally cannot validate the current price. [DATA] The real driver was oil: Brent ran from ~$76.80 on 2026-07-10 to above $100 intraday on 2026-07-24 after Houthi forces declared a naval blockade on Saudi Arabia and claimed attacks on two Saudi tankers on 2026-07-22, with Trump saying on 7/23 the US would hold Iran responsible. [DATA] Brent then fell 3.9% Friday to settle $96.78, its biggest one-day drop since late June, on reports of a possible path to resumed US-Iran talks. [DATA] RSI(14) is 84.0. [ASSUMED] Adding into an 84 RSI on a risk premium that just showed its first crack would be chasing; going to zero into a live conflict with tankers under attack would leave the rest of the book naked to an oil shock. A 4% hold is the honest middle — I have no edge on whether Washington escalates, and I am sizing to that admission rather than dressing it up as a view.
rationale.CVX: Cut from ~10.4% to 4%, same logic as XOM and rather more urgent. [DATA] CVX closed 194.72 with an RSI(14) of 92.0 — the single most overbought reading anywhere in the 100-name universe this tick — after rising in six of the last seven sessions. [DATA] Its Q2 report on 2026-07-31 covers the same pre-spike April-June quarter as Exxon's. [ASSUMED] I am deliberately declining to cite the widely-quoted consensus EPS figures for either major: the $5.79 quoted for CVX and $3.88 for XOM are implausible against trailing-twelve-month EPS of roughly $6.10 and $6.37, implied by Robinhood's P/E of 31.91 and 24.63 at Friday's closes — a single quarter cannot plausibly equal a full trailing year. I treat those consensus numbers as unreliable and build no thesis on them rather than repeating a figure I cannot reconcile. [ASSUMED] Held at 4% purely as the second leg of the escalation hedge. The pair is now 8% of the book, down from 16.8%, which correctly reflects that the oil trade has become a risk position rather than a conviction one.

risks: PYPL is 38% of deployed capital and carries a binary M&A outcome: if Stripe/Advent publicly walk away, the stock plausibly retraces toward the $47.37 close of 2026-07-14 before the bid leaked, roughly 16% down on the position. Whether a revised bid has actually been submitted is UNVERIFIED — no source confirmed one, and nothing in this thesis assumes it.

Cutting META to zero before its 2026-07-29 print is a directional bet against a company that could simply beat and hold capex flat, in which case the book forgoes a rebound in a name already 25% below its 52-week high of 796.25. The capex-punishment pattern is five observations over roughly a week, not a law.

63% cash is a heavy drag if the 2026-07-29 FOMC reads dovish and the four mega-cap prints (META and MSFT 7/29, AAPL and AMZN 7/30) clear the AI-capex fear rather than deepen it. This book is already -12.7% from inception and cash alone cannot repair that.

The energy cut is the mirror risk: if US military action against Iran escalates and Brent decisively takes out $100, an 8% energy weight badly underhedges the rest of the book. Friday's 3.9% Brent decline may be noise rather than the start of a fade — the brief was explicit that the premium is 'not yet a confirmed fade'.
LLY at a 42.09 trailing P/E has no valuation cushion; a guidance stumble on 2026-08-05 or an adverse turn in the Novo litigation would hit a position sized on the assumption that neither happens.

The BAC trim is being made at what is currently the best price the book has ever seen for the name (52-week high set this session). If the dividend raise starts a re-rating rather than capping one, the trim is early.

reflection.looking_back: The 7/22 book carried eight names (BAC 10%, CVX 10%, META 8%, LLY 8%, PYPL 8%, XOM 8%, REGN 6%, GOOGL 2%) and queued cuts to GOOGL and REGN. Marked across the two sessions to 7/24 the book went $87.35 to $87.28, -0.07%, while SPY fell from 747.41 to 738.85, -1.15%. That is alpha of +1.08 points — the book's best relative result in several ticks — and it came almost entirely from what it did not own. Seven of the eight holdings finished green; META (-5.10%) and GOOGL (-6.52%) were the only drags, together costing -0.71 points.
worked: Cutting GOOGL once its event fired was vindicated hard: GOOGL fell a further 6.52% across the two sessions (342.09 to 319.77), including -7.13% on 7/23 alone — its worst session in 14 months — after raising FY26 capex to $195-205B. The queued sell fills at the 7/23 open of 321.13.

Owning none of the AI-capex complex was the single largest contributor: INTC -7.90% (7/24), TSLA -14.52% (7/23) and ORCL -4.19% to a 52-week low (7/24) were the three worst large-cap wrecks of the window and the book held zero of them.
The energy sleeve did its job in a down tape: XOM +1.61% and CVX +0.90% across two sessions while SPY fell 1.15%.
BAC's flat hold was rewarded on 7/24 by a 14% dividend raise to $0.32 that carried it to a 52-week high of 62.275 — the fundamental confirmation the prior tick had argued for, arriving on schedule.
missed: META was left at 7.4% and cost -0.40 points. The PRIOR reflection had already named META as 'AI-capex sympathy risk from GOOGL's reaction' and then held it anyway. The diagnosis was right and the trade did not follow — that is the expensive kind of miss, because the information was already in hand and cost real money.

The energy thesis was stated wrongly. It was framed as a bet on dated 7/31 earnings, but the actual driver was a geopolitical oil spike (Brent ~$76.80 on 7/10 to above $100 intraday on 7/24). That matters beyond bookkeeping: because the 7/31 reports cover April-June, before the spike, the stated catalyst could never have validated the position — which means the exit signal would have been missed too.

XOM and CVX were allowed to run to RSI 84 and 92 with no trim rule at all. A 16.8% combined weight in the two most overbought names in the universe was a sizing failure that only luck kept from hurting this tick.
reflection.adjustment: Act on the diagnosis in the same tick it is made. META goes to zero BEFORE its 7/29 print rather than being flagged as a risk and held for a third consecutive tick. And stop calling the energy pair an earnings trade: the 7/31 prints cover a pre-spike quarter, so XOM/CVX are cut from 16.8% to an 8% escalation hedge, with the RSI 84 and 92 readings treated as a reason to trim rather than a detail to note in passing.
